edges.description: Tick inoculation exposes local dermal macrophages and dendritic cells to rickettsiae.
Local infection at the tick attachment site produces a necrotic eschar.
Dermal infection spreads through lymphatic vessels to draining lymph nodes.
Rickettsiae occupy the host-cell cytosol after entry.
Infection of draining nodes contributes to regional lymphadenopathy near the eschar.
Lymphatic and hematogenous spread seeds systemic endothelial infection.
Cytosolic R. heilongjiangensis remains dependent on bacterial ribosomal translation.
Disseminated rickettsiae infect endothelial cells and trigger vasculitic injury.
R. heilongjiangensis infection elicits endothelial Tim-3 responses that promote nitric-oxide-mediated killing.
Systemic endothelial infection and inflammation drive the acute febrile syndrome.
Cutaneous small-vessel inflammation produces a macular or maculopapular eruption.

nodes.description: After cutaneous inoculation, spotted-fever-group rickettsiae first infect CD68-positive macrophage or dendritic cells in the skin before reaching draining nodes and systemic endothelial targets.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenesis of Rickettsial Diseases: Pathogenic and Immune Mechanisms of an Endotheliotropic Infection.
evidence.snippet: The initial target cells of infection are CD68+ cells (macrophages and/or dendritic cells)

nodes.description: Doxycycline is the empiric treatment for Far Eastern spotted fever because it penetrates cells and blocks bacterial ribosomal translation in the intracytosolic Rickettsia compartment.

evidence.reference_title: Acute tick-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia heilongjiangensis in Russian Far East.
evidence.snippet: | Doxycycline treatment, 100 mg twice daily for 14 d | 13 |

nodes.description: In R. heilongjiangensis infection, Tim-3 expression in endothelial cells promotes inducible nitric oxide synthase and nitric-oxide-dependent intracellular killing during early infection.

biological_processes: positive regulation of nitric oxide biosynthetic process

evidence.reference_title: Enhanced Expression of T-Cell Immunoglobulin and Mucin Domain Protein 3 in Endothelial Cells Facilitates Intracellular Killing of Rickettsia heilongjiangensis.
evidence.snippet: These results reveal that enhanced Tim-3 expression facilitates intracellular rickettsial killing in a nitric oxide-dependent manner in endothelial cells during the early phase of rickettsial infection.

nodes.description: Fever is part of the acute systemic FESF syndrome.

evidence.snippet: After an incubation period of 4 to 7 days, the patient had a sudden onset with fever, but no specific symptoms appeared during the first several days.

nodes.description: A necrotic eschar forms at the tick attachment site in most FESF cases.

evidence.reference_title: Acute tick-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia heilongjiangensis in Russian Far East.

evidence.snippet: A case of Rickettsia heilongjiangensis infection in Japan was identified in a 35-year-old man who had rash, fever, and eschars.

nodes.description: Rickettsia organisms escape into the host-cell cytosol and exploit intracellular metabolites, so effective treatment must reach a cytosolic bacterial compartment in endothelial and mononuclear phagocyte targets.

biological_processes: biological process involved in interaction with host

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenesis of Rickettsial Diseases: Pathogenic and Immune Mechanisms of an Endotheliotropic Infection.
evidence.snippet: Residing free in the cytosol of the host cell, they acquire many necessary components via transport mechanisms instead of maintaining genes for synthesizing sugars, lipids, nucleotides, and amino acids.

evidence.reference_title: Enhanced Expression of T-Cell Immunoglobulin and Mucin Domain Protein 3 in Endothelial Cells Facilitates Intracellular Killing of Rickettsia heilongjiangensis.
evidence.snippet: T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain protein 3 (Tim-3) is expressed in human vascular endothelial cells, the major target cells of rickettsiae.

nodes.description: Rickettsiae leave the inoculation site through dermal lymphatic vessels and reach the regional draining lymph nodes.

evidence.snippet: The rickettsiae then spread via lymphatic vessels to the regional lymph nodes

nodes.description: A macular or maculopapular rash usually appears a few days after fever onset.

evidence.reference_title: Acute tick-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia heilongjiangensis in Russian Far East.

nodes.description: Avoiding tick bites, using effective skin repellents, wearing permethrin-treated outer clothing, and removing attached ticks promptly reduce the tick exposure that triggers Far Eastern spotted fever.

evidence.snippet: The best method to avoid tick bites is twofold: application of a topical deet (N,N-diethyl-m-toluamide) repellent to exposed skin, and treatment of clothing with permethrin.

nodes.description: Regional lymph-node enlargement can accompany the inoculation eschar.

evidence.reference_title: Acute tick-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia heilongjiangensis in Russian Far East.

nodes.description: R. heilongjiangensis depends on bacterial ribosomal translation; doxycycline exploits this conserved bacterial vulnerability to arrest rickettsial protein synthesis.

evidence.reference_title: Ribosome-targeting antibiotics and mechanisms of bacterial resistance.
evidence.snippet: The ribosome is one of the main antibiotic targets in the bacterial cell.

nodes.description: Disseminated rickettsial infection injures vascular endothelium, increases vascular permeability, and produces the rash and edema-centered tissue injury characteristic of spotted-fever-group rickettsioses.

evidence.reference_title: Host-cell interactions with pathogenic Rickettsia species.
evidence.snippet: It is now well established that a majority of sequelae associated with human rickettsioses are the outcome of the pathogen's affinity for endothelium lining the blood vessels, the consequences of which are vascular inflammation, insult to vascular integrity and compromised vascular permeability, collectively termed 'Rickettsial vasculitis'.

nodes.description: Infected Haemaphysalis ticks inject R. conorii subsp. heilongjiangensis into skin while feeding, seeding local rickettsial infection at the bite site.

evidence.reference_title: Acute tick-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia heilongjiangensis in Russian Far East.
evidence.snippet: Five to 20 days before onset of the disease, most patients reported tick bites or tick exposure.
